confirmed: The entire 320-line markdown and all nine PDF pages were read. source.version correctly identifies the IJCAI-25 published proceedings, Special Track on Human-Centred AI, printed pp. 10280-10288; the title and four authors match. No appendix is present or supplementary material identified in this document (PDF pp. 1-9; title/affiliations on p. 1, References on pp. 7-9).

The main study explicitly randomly assigns people between five conditions: Control, Early-AI Labeled, Early-AI Unlabeled, Late-AI Labeled, and Late-AI Unlabeled. Participants generate and refine plastic-pollution solutions, with GPT-4 suggestions supplied according to condition; experts score their output. has_randomized_people_study is true, and referral to the two-screener pipeline is warranted (PDF p. 3, sections 3.1-3.4; p. 4, section 3.5).

The online_rct classification is supported by random assignment and task administration on a custom web platform. The paper describes a convenience sample of adults without naming an online recruitment panel or participant country; the observational, ai_vs_human, and synthesis context classes do not apply (PDF p. 3, sections 3.1-3.3; p. 7, section 5).

The stated final sample is 247 people: Control 50, Early-AI Labeled 49, Early-AI Unlabeled 49, Late-AI Labeled 50, and Late-AI Unlabeled 49. These are people, not ideas or ratings; the study exceeds the 50-person threshold across arms even though some individual arms have 49 people (PDF p. 3, section 3.1).

Section 3.1 reports 254 initially enrolled, seven excluded, and a final 247, then describes random assignment using the final arm counts. It does not separately identify a pre-exclusion randomized total or pre-exclusion arm counts, so leaving those counts null avoids equating enrollment with randomization (PDF p. 3, section 3.1).

The form correctly flags the unreconciled sample-size issue: the stated final sample is 247, while the reported one-way ANOVAs use F(4, 237). Section 3.6 describes outlier and incomplete-response screening without additional counts; no replacement analyzed count should be back-calculated (PDF p. 3, section 3.1; p. 4, sections 3.6 and 4.1).

GPT-4 supplied two or three suggestions of 30 to 50 words. Early groups received them with the first-round prompt, late groups at the second round, and the control received none; labels were AI-generated ideas or Ideas from others. Each ideation round lasted 5-7 minutes (PDF p. 3, sections 3.3-3.4; p. 4, Figure 1; p. 7, section 5).

Three domain experts independently scored final ideas on novelty, usefulness, and originality using 7-point scales, with intraclass correlation ? 0.80. These are scored-output measures, so criterion 3 is met; the exact formula combining components into the reported overall creativity score is not specified (PDF p. 4, section 3.5).

Every number in S1-O1.reported and one_line_finding matches: Early-AI-Labeled M = 6.01, SD = 0.48; Control M = 4.94; omnibus F(4, 237) = 37.54, p < .001, partial ?? = .38. The text also reports both Early-AI groups above the Late-AI groups and Control; the omnibus test is not mislabeled as a pairwise test in the form (PDF p. 4, section 4.1).

Every number in S1-O2.reported matches the labeled-versus-unlabeled comparison: semantic distance .61 vs. .73, t = ?11.04, p < .001, d = 1.58. The paper prints a positive d despite the negative t; the form preserves that reported value (PDF p. 5, section 4.2).

Semantic alignment uses text-embedding-ada-002 and cosine similarity between each participant submission and each supplied AI suggestion, with lower distances indicating stronger overlap. It is not a comparison across different participants, so construct other and question with_ai are appropriate; the paper does not explicitly establish removal of previously shown suggestions (PDF p. 4, sections 3.4-3.5).

The stimulus-development pilot is reported only as n = 15, without an explicit sampling unit, random-assignment statement, assistance comparison, or separate participant-output results. It does not establish an additional randomized people study with fewer than 50 analyzed participants (PDF p. 3, section 3.3).

This document reports an original experiment, not a synthesis; the empty synthesis fields correctly avoid inventing study counts, pooled effects, intervals, or standardizers (PDF pp. 3-5, sections 3-4).
summary: The paper reports a randomized five-condition study with 247 analyzed adults and expert-scored ideas, requiring the two-screener pipeline. The source version and recorded main statistics are supported, but the form omits component outcomes, leaves the exclusions field blank, and incorrectly records no company involvement.
